One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A family of contactors rips of

Summary:
A new sparkling pool is what you’re promised, what you get is a hole in the ground if you’re lucky – sometimes they just pockets your deposits and does a duck.

ANOTHER SCAMSTER TO CATCH OUT :)

Further information:
The De Bruyn Brothers' MO is simple: Take a deposit, start some work, don’t finish the job! Leaving clients with a ghastly pit in their gardens when they were dreaming of a sparkling pool.

People have been ripped off between R30 000 to R220 000.

CASE STUDY - ELAINE & FAMILY - BOKSBURG - PAID R33000 FOR A POOL.
We have acquired the services of DB Landscape. Promised the kids a pool for Christmas and got a pit. We also paid a deposit in Dec 2015 for a pool and the left an open hole and rubble to date - it's a hazard and she fears that her kids could get hurt. I cannot get hold of them.

CASE STUDY - ETTIENE - ALBERTON - PAID R220 000 for a pool and landscaping
Left with a massive hole in the garden - they built a couple of flower beds and a small wall with Ettiene's bricks and then did a duck. The work carried out is worth about R48 000.

Have a list of at least 15 cases of people that have been done in - all the same MO.We will do a group meeting with some at least 5 additional case studies at Herman's house

We've tracked them down in Meyerton and have set up a sting to catch them.

Press Release:


Pool Con Artists
They promise a sparkling new pool, then duck with the deposit, leaving nothing but a big hole in the ground and in your pocket. Several trusting home owners have fallen victim to a family-run “outdoor development” business whose slick presentations have earned them hundreds of thousands for very little work done. Carte Blanche follows the trail of two conniving contractors.


Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: A sparkling pool is an investment for many South Africans. It’s one of those home improvement projects that people aspire to and many painstakingly save towards.

ELAINE: I wanted an environment that is safe for my kids, but also to create a fun environment for them.

VO: Elaine Motsaone decided on De Bruyn Landscape Consultants to build her dream pool. The one-stop landscaping and pool building company run by brothers Armand and Marius.

ELAINE: Profile was attractive, looked at pics and it was exactly what I wantedmy yard to look like….

LINK: It’s boom time for contractors, but beware there are those that will take you for a ride.

VO: It was a R33 000 ride for Elaine.

After paying the deposit, it took some hounding before any workers made an appearance at the Motsoane’s home in Boksburg.

ELAINE: They came at 09.00 and were gone by 15.30 – and they came for the next two days – and this was it.
Bongani: They just dug this hole and that was it?
ELAINE: Yes.
BONGANI: You could have dug this hole by yourself?
ELAINE: I guess we could have.

VO: Gayle Martin saved R50 000 for her family’s dream pool over three years – this is what they got…

GAYLE: it’s awful Bongani, as I say, it’s an enormous amount money // The structure is not complete as you can see, and at the moment it’s just collecting mosquito larwa.

VO: The De Bruyn Brothers' modus operandi is simple: They sell you a dream with their slick presentations.

Herman Putter from Waterfall Estate in Midrand says he fell hook, line and sinker in 2014, for the De Bruyn’s con. They targetted his Estate during the construction phase.

HERMAN: as you can see the proposal is designed very nicely, it’s very graphic, it’s professional….details of the company, offices… sales… looking very legit…
BONGANI: Yah, I’d buy it, I’d want these guys to do my garden…
HERMAN: IF you look at this, it is incredibly impressive

VO: He paid close to R300 000 for landscaping, decking and a pool – although some work was done, it was an uphill battle.

HERMAN: On a daily basis we would phone them – we would try and get them here, he blamed everything under the sun.

VO: Tracey-Lee van Tonder worked at De Bruyns as their operations secretary, dealing with upset clients day in and day out – she says it was her job to keep them at bay.

TRACEY-LEE: Armand told me you have to keep the clients of my back, please!
BONGANI: did they look bothered that people were complaining about them?
TRACEY-LEE: Not at all, not at all.They were blaze about that

VO: Eventually Herman gave up and brought in other contractors to complete the job. But he was not the only one to be seduce by De Bruyns’ presentation. He managed to track down at least 8 more upset customers.

Richard Riche paid R40 000

RICHARD: They created a huge hole in the garden that took them over a month to do.

VO: THSIDI MAWELA parted with R103 000….

TSHIDI: All I have to show is: a big hole and 1000 bricks….. I called them several times and from there they were nowhere to be found.

VO: Tracey-Lee says while deals were coming in during the three months of her employment – cash was scarce.

TRACEY-LEE: Most of the time their wasn’t funding for petrol money to send someone to site. That’s why I don’t know // where’s the deposit money going to?
HERMAN: the fact that after receiveing a deposit of R200 000 within one week again they didn’t have money – they had to waste it somewhere and it was definitely not on gardening equipment and plants.
BONGANI: We’re the De Bruyn brothers broke?
TRACEY-LEE: Not at all, not at all, they weren’t.

VO: They seem to be doing pretty well for themselves, Armand De Bruyn lives at an upmarket security complex in Three Rivers, in a large double story unit.

LINK: we’ve established they have an office in Meyerton and it appears that they are still operating from there – so we are going to go see if we can find them. CAR LINK

UPSOUND CONFRONT:
BONGANI: Hello,
MARTIE: Take the camera out of my face….
BONGANI: I’m looking for Armand and Marius de Bruyn – Are they here?
MARTIE: No they are not here.

VO: With the De Bruyn Brothers nowhere to be seen, we left their offices. Armand committed to do a telephonic interview the next day.

BONGANI: I’ve seen a difference between what the presentations that your clients said you gave to them were and the actualy job you did for them – what’s gone wrong there?
ARMAND: According to me, nothing has gone wrong – what I promised them that is what I delivered.
BONGANI: What you promised them is what you delivered?
ARMAND: Yes…

VO: Ettienne Bester, from Eye of Africa in Alberton, would strongly disagree. He paid the De Bruyns a deposit of R220 000 in July 2015 – he’s left with a sandpit of a garden and a brick structure in the ground for a pool.

BONGANI: This is the pool?
ETTIENNE: That is what we got. It’s far too deep – and very impractical – there’s no way that any cleaning equipment can go from the bottom to the top here.

VO: Often the value of the completed work is nowhere near the value of the deposit paid.

ETTIENNE: We did an estimate on the work that was done – the work that was done is about 20% of the amount that we paid.

VO: Gayle says the only thing they managed to do with her R50 000, was to rob her grandchildren of their Christmas present.

GAYLE: the children had gotten their pool noodles, people were coming for Christmas – we were going to wet the pool’s head so to speak.

VO: Barry Vorster is from the National Spa and Pool Institute.

BARRY: it’s a mess, it’s the type of thing someone would attempt to build themselves, a real homemade, backyard job.
BONGANI: What’s wrong with it?
BARRY: Everything, the concrete work is below standard, the re-inforcing is below standard, finishing is below standard, the concrete mixing is inconsistent, the sides are scew, the levels are out…
BONGANI: it’s a disaster
BaRRY: yah, it’s a disaster.

VO: A side from the upset clients, suppliers were also unhappy says former employee Tracey-Lee.

TRACEY-LEE: Accounts dept handled money, enven now suppliers [phone me afterward for their money – I just tell them I don’t work there any more and I don’t know what to say to them.

VO: We tracked down some of these Gauteng based suppliers.

Steven Warren supplied rubble skips at a cost of R1500.

UPSOUND EASY SKIPS: As a small business operator whilst the money might seem a small amount, but for the one man band, it’s crucial

VO: Marius Engelbrecht lost 6 grand..

UPSOUND MARIUS ENGELBRECHT: INT 2 M2 he just never paid me // I removed all this rubble for him, I sent the invoices and he never responded.

VO: But there are even bigger amounts outstanding - Sebenza farms in KZN are owed R85 000.

These types of conmen are a dime a dozen in the swimming pool industry says Barry

BARRY: We call them bakkie and bucket brigades, they start a project, they don’t really know what they are doing, they are not qualified – take a huge deposit and then disappear.

VO: And that’s just what the De Bruyn brothers did, says Gayle.

GAYLE: Between the two of them – they just evaporated

LINK: it’s classic hit and run because what used to be a fantastic website with beautiful pictures and all the bells and whistles, is now under construction. These guys seem impossible to reach, their business phones are disconnected and it appears they are exiting the industy. RUNNER LINK

VO: It should be an easy exit - It seems De Bruyn Landscape Consultants is not a registered company nor have they registered to pay VAT – despite charging for it.

BONGANI: Are you VAT registered?
ARMAND: No comment on that
BONGANI: Did you pay over the VAT that you were charging the clients?
ARMAND: I have no comment on that.
BONGANI: I have at least 8 invoices…
ARMAND: Bongani, Bongani, let stick to the original agreement and deal with the complaints
BONGANI: Well these are the complaints, this is part of the complaint, the clients are saying that you are claiming you are about to be liquidated, they say that you charged them VAT…
ARMAND: Bongani… INT 1 M11 // I have the right to answer what ever I feel comfortable with… INT 1 M12

VO: We moved onto the projects – Armand claimed that Elaine’s project was delayed because the company closed for holidays in December

BONGANI: Are you going to finish the pool?
ARMAND: Bongani, we are closing the company down and I think I am going to close this company down and I am going to end the conversation with you guys by saying that.
BONGANI: Armand, that’s not good enough. You’ve taken people’s money, you haven’t compelted the jobs and it’s not good enough to say you are closing the company down.

VO: He eventually cut the call.

Armand’s upset clients are not surprised by his response, but they say they will never be seduced by slick presentations again.

HERMAN: if you can’t speak to the customers of previous projects personally – move on. do not pay deposits – work with bigger compnay that can pay for the equipment andmaterials themselves. It is a bit more money – but it is more than worth it in the long run.

VO: Armand later sent a written response with his version of events, mainly blaming his clients for the delays that prevented him from completing the work.

They deny his allegations. But it will be for the courts to decide as they have started with legal procedings.

GAYLE: It’s devastating to put your trust in someone who you thought had your better interest at heart and then to be taken for a ride.

ETTIENNE: Armand De Bruyn and Marius De Bruyn are conninng people out of their money // but with them the intent is never there to finish the project –definitely like to see them behind bars – because they are criminals. INT 7 M3
















PROMOS

PROMO 1 - 10 seconds
VO: Summer Scamters promise sparkling pools, but deliver big holes and make off with the cash.

ETTIENNE: That is what we got. It’s far too deep – and very impractical. INT 8


PROMO 2 – 15 seconds
VO: With Summer in full swing, it’s boom time for dodgy conmen are ready to take you for a ride.

BARRY: We call them bakkie and bucket brigades, they start a project, they don’t really know what they are doing.

VO: We expose a dodgy company.

PROMO 3 `– 15 seconds
VO: A dodgy outdoor developer makes off with hundreds of thousands of rands – leaving clients with giant pits and out of pocket.

HERMAN: After receiveing a deposit of R200 000 within one week again they didn’t have money – they had to waste it somewhere and it was definitely not on gardening equipment and plants.

ETTIENNE: We did an estimate on the work that was done – the work that was done is about 20% of the amount that we paid. VO: Gayle says the only thing they managed to do with her R50 000, was to rob her grandchildren of their Christmas present. GAYLE: the children had gotten their pool noodles, people were coming for Christmas – we were going to wet the pool’s head so to speak. VO: Barry Vorster is from the National Spa and Pool Institute. BARRY: it’s a mess, it’s the type of thing someone would attempt to build themselves, a real homemade, backyard job. BONGANI: What’s wrong with it? BARRY: Everything, the concrete work is below standard, the re-inforcing is below standard, finishing is below standard, the concrete mixing is inconsistent, the sides are scew, the levels are out… BONGANI: it’s a disaster BaRRY: yah, it’s a disaster. VO: A side from the upset clients, suppliers were also unhappy says former employee Tracey-Lee. TRACEY-LEE: Accounts dept handled money, enven now suppliers [phone me afterward for their money – I just tell them I don’t work there any more and I don’t know what to say to them. VO: We tracked down some of these Gauteng based suppliers. Steven Warren supplied rubble skips at a cost of R1500. UPSOUND EASY SKIPS: As a small business operator whilst the money might seem a small amount, but for the one man band, it’s crucial VO: Marius Engelbrecht lost 6 grand.. UPSOUND MARIUS ENGELBRECHT: INT 2 M2 he just never paid me // I removed all this rubble for him, I sent the invoices and he never responded. VO: But there are even bigger amounts outstanding - Sebenza farms in KZN are owed R85 000. These types of conmen are a dime a dozen in the swimming pool industry says Barry BARRY: We call them bakkie and bucket brigades, they start a project, they don’t really know what they are doing, they are not qualified – take a huge deposit and then disappear. VO: And that’s just what the De Bruyn brothers did, says Gayle. GAYLE: Between the two of them – they just evaporated LINK: it’s classic hit and run because what used to be a fantastic website with beautiful pictures and all the bells and whistles, is now under construction. These guys seem impossible to reach, their business phones are disconnected and it appears they are exiting the industy. RUNNER LINK VO: It should be an easy exit - It seems De Bruyn Landscape Consultants is not a registered company nor have they registered to pay VAT – despite charging for it. BONGANI: Are you VAT registered? ARMAND: No comment on that BONGANI: Did you pay over the VAT that you were charging the clients? ARMAND: I have no comment on that. BONGANI: I have at least 8 invoices… ARMAND: Bongani, Bongani, let stick to the original agreement and deal with the complaints BONGANI: Well these are the complaints, this is part of the complaint, the clients are saying that you are claiming you are about to be liquidated, they say that you charged them VAT… ARMAND: Bongani… INT 1 M11 // I have the right to answer what ever I feel comfortable with… INT 1 M12 VO: We moved onto the projects – Armand claimed that Elaine’s project was delayed because the company closed for holidays in December BONGANI: Are you going to finish the pool? ARMAND: Bongani, we are closing the company down and I think I am going to close this company down and I am going to end the conversation with you guys by saying that. BONGANI: Armand, that’s not good enough. You’ve taken people’s money, you haven’t compelted the jobs and it’s not good enough to say you are closing the company down. VO: He eventually cut the call. Armand’s upset clients are not surprised by his response, but they say they will never be seduced by slick presentations again. HERMAN: if you can’t speak to the customers of previous projects personally – move on. do not pay deposits – work with bigger compnay that can pay for the equipment andmaterials themselves. It is a bit more money – but it is more than worth it in the long run. VO: Armand later sent a written response with his version of events, mainly blaming his clients for the delays that prevented him from completing the work. They deny his allegations. But it will be for the courts to decide as they have started with legal procedings. GAYLE: It’s devastating to put your trust in someone who you thought had your better interest at heart and then to be taken for a ride. ETTIENNE: Armand De Bruyn and Marius De Bruyn are conninng people out of their money // but with them the intent is never there to finish the project –definitely like to see them behind bars – because they are criminals. INT 7 M3 PROMOS PROMO 1 - 10 seconds VO: Summer Scamters promise sparkling pools, but deliver big holes and make off with the cash. ETTIENNE: That is what we got. It’s far too deep – and very impractical. INT 8 PROMO 2 – 15 seconds VO: With Summer in full swing, it’s boom time for dodgy conmen are ready to take you for a ride. BARRY: We call them bakkie and bucket brigades, they start a project, they don’t really know what they are doing. VO: We expose a dodgy company. PROMO 3 `– 15 seconds VO: A dodgy outdoor developer makes off with hundreds of thousands of rands – leaving clients with giant pits and out of pocket. HERMAN: After receiveing a deposit of R200 000 within one week again they didn’t have money – they had to waste it somewhere and it was definitely not on gardening equipment and plants. metadata.Summary: A new sparkling pool is what you’re promised, what you get is a hole in the ground if you’re lucky – sometimes they just pockets your deposits and does a duck. ANOTHER SCAMSTER TO CATCH OUT :)
metadata.Further information: The De Bruyn Brothers' MO is simple: Take a deposit, start some work, don’t finish the job! Leaving clients with a ghastly pit in their gardens when they were dreaming of a sparkling pool. People have been ripped off between R30 000 to R220 000. CASE STUDY - ELAINE & FAMILY - BOKSBURG - PAID R33000 FOR A POOL. We have acquired the services of DB Landscape. Promised the kids a pool for Christmas and got a pit. We also paid a deposit in Dec 2015 for a pool and the left an open hole and rubble to date - it's a hazard and she fears that her kids could get hurt. I cannot get hold of them. CASE STUDY - ETTIENE - ALBERTON - PAID R220 000 for a pool and landscaping Left with a massive hole in the garden - they built a couple of flower beds and a small wall with Ettiene's bricks and then did a duck. The work carried out is worth about R48 000. CASE STUDY - HERMAN PUTTER - PAID THEM AROUND R400 000 - eventually got most of the work done He has made it his mission to alert people about their dodgy dealings and have investigated the De Bruyn Brothers. Have a list of at least 15 cases of people that have been done in - all the same MO.We will do a group meeting with some at least 5 additional case studies at Herman's house We've tracked them down in Meyerton and have set up a sting to catch them. INterview the National Spa and Pool Institute of South Africa - as experts what can people look out for - we get them to look at one of the pool and give their expert opinion on the quality of work. The first sound up doesn’t work too sudden – can you start introducing the issue more in script Dont mention we all need pools Can you put the name of each brother under their photos Subtitles promised them, Saying that to you guys. We are Let’s stick to SCRIPT: Besides the upset clients – should be Aside from the upset clients You refer to these types of conmen – who are the men in the shot? Although there are shades of truth all the clients deny his allegations. PAMELA: Satisfied no legal issues
